title: Rams' Puka Nacua suspended three games, will serve ban during injured reserve stint - CBS Sports
description: The NFL threatened Nacua with potential "banishment" from the league for future violations of the personal conduc
body:
The NFL threatened Nacua with potential "banishment" from the league for future violations of the personal conduct policy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Nacua's suspension takes effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14, after the Rams' key divisional game against the San Francisco 49ers.Nacua is set to miss three high-stakes matchups against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and 49ers before he is eligible to return on December 20, in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.The NFL did not publicly disclose the nature of Nacua's personal conduct policy violation. It can be inferred, however, that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.The woman filed a temporary restraining order against Nacua in March. The lawsuit also mentioned allegations of gender violence and assault and battery. Nacua's attorney denied the allegations and said this is a "blackmail" attempt from the alleged victim on December 31, 2025.
According to ESPN, the NFL said it communicated to Nacua that "any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league."As unfortunate as the suspension is for Nacua, the timing is convenient. The Rams placed him on injured reserve on November 12 due to his PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, so he was already set to miss at least four games during his recovery. Players may serve suspensions while on injured reserve, so he will complete the three-game ban during the remainder of his minimum IR stint. While suspended, Nacua will not be allowed in the team facilities, meaning he will not be allowed to rehab his injury with the team until the suspension is over. Previous instances of players serving suspensions while on injured reserve include Daniel Ekuale (2025), Sam Williams (2024), Mike Woods (2023), and David Parry (2018).
Puka Nacua absence timelineWeek 10: Placed on IR, missed game vs. CardinalsWeek 11: Suspension begins, remains on IR, Rams on byeWeek 12: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game vs. PackersWeek 13: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game vs. ChiefsWeek 14: Suspension continues, remains on IR, will miss game at 49ersWeek 15: Suspension to be lifted, eligible for reinstatement from IR, can play game vs. CowboysNacua already missed two games this season due to a hip injury, and the Rams went 1-1 in his absence in Weeks 2 and 3 against the New York Giants and Denver Broncos. Davante Adams stepped up in a big way as the team's No. 1 receiver and racked up 332 yards in those contests. Adams remains in the midst of his recovery from a hamstring injury but could return for the Rams' battle with the Packers, which would put him back at the top of the receiving pecking order.When he is on the field, Nacua remains a top-flight wide receiver. He averages 102.1 yards per game this year, which is high enough to make him the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards per game at 96.2 over his career.Nacua has been a massive piece of the Rams' offensive game plan and saw at least seven targets in each of his first seven games of the year. He amassed a whopping 24 targets in Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills, which were the most by any player in a single game since 2009.

title: House GOP leaders plan December push for Protect College Sports Act - CBS Sports
description: Both the House and Senate must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, or the process star
body:
Both the House and Senate must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, or the process starts over in a Congress controlled by Democrats
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:02 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College sports legislation that much of Washington had already buried is getting new life as lobbying efforts and negotiations over potential changes kicked into high gear this week.On Thursday, House Republican leaders gave the Protect College Sports Act something it hadn't yet had: a target date.House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Education and Workforce Committee chairman Tim Walberg and Energy and Commerce Committee chairman Brett Guthrie said in a joint statement Thursday they plan to bring the landmark college sports bill to the House floor the first week of December, just in time for conference championship weekend."College sports are at a crossroad and Congress needs to pass strong antitrust protections to end the Wild West atmosphere that exists today," the three Republicans said. "We are committed to getting a bill to President Trump's desk that saves college sports."
The leadership also acknowledged the PCSA "in its current form faces real challenges in the House from many factions of our conference who take issue with several measures in the bill, along with Democrats outright opposing it.""We are working with our members to address as many issues as possible while keeping those changes narrow in order to maintain the fragile coalitions in the House and Senate," the statement said.Any change to the PCSA sends the bill back to the Senate, which passed it 77-22 on Sept. 28, and would require the chamber to vote on it again. The window is shrinking by the day, lending credence to the prospect that the bill will never pass. Both chambers must finish business before the new Congress is sworn in Jan. 3, or the process starts over in a Congress controlled by Democrats. The House's last scheduled day of work is Dec. 17, and government funding expires Dec. 11.
Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell and New York Yankees president Randy Levine, President Trump's strongest advocates for the bill outside Washington, D.C., spent Thursday on Capitol Hill. Sources tell CBS Sports that Big Ten commissioner Tony Pettiti is also lobbying heavily for the bill. Campbell, the Texas Tech board chairman whose Saving College Sports group is running a multimillion-dollar ad campaign during college football broadcasts, and Levine, the New York Yankees president and vice chair of President Trump's college sports roundtable, have led the outside push for the bill. A source close to Campbell said backers continue to believe the PCSA has broad enough support to pass the House and are encouraged by Scalise's commitment to a vote.Levine was blunter in a letter to House members last week. "History will remember if you choose wrong," he wrote. "Pass the PCSA."
Scalise has been among the most prominent Republican skeptics of the PCSA and a supporter of the SCORE Act, the House's own college sports bill, which leadership pulled from the floor three times earlier this year. He previously said the PCSA's neutrality on whether athletes can be employees would need to be addressed through amendments.But the objections run deeper than one provision in the 171-page bill, which would give schools, conferences and the NCAA targeted antitrust protection to enforce rules on athlete pay, eligibility and transfers, while also preempting patchwork state NIL laws and raising the revenue-sharing cap to $48.8 million per school.One of the biggest obstacles is a provision that caps power conferences at 20 members and restricts coaches from being hired away by other schools during the season.
Twenty-one House Republicans objected to that 20-member cap and to a three-year waiting period for schools that switch leagues in an Oct. 2 letter. Many hail from states with ACC schools that have actively sought exit plans from the conference.Florida Rep. Byron Donalds, the state's governor-elect, said last week: "I hate that bill."Others want an outright ban on classifying athletes as employees and a cap on international players. Walberg, one of three House leaders to announce their intention to push the bill forward Thursday, held a press conference Wednesday to discuss his own legislation, the TEAM USA Act, which would limit international players to 20 percent of varsity rosters.
The biggest obstacle might be the Democrats. The Congressional Black Caucus condemned the bill the day after the Senate vote, citing HBCU funding, the lack of employment rights for athletes and limits on their ability to sue. Democrats, who won control of both chambers in the Nov. 3 midterms, also have little incentive to hand the outgoing Republican majority a win. Republicans currently hold a 218-214 edge in the lame-duck House.Sen. Ted Cruz, the bill's lead Republican author, has been negotiating with House Democrats, Front Office Sports reported Wednesday. One idea on the table, either in the bill or as separate legislation, is a pathway to student loan forgiveness for HBCU attendees.Meanwhile, conferences are actively working on self-governance models to better police eligibility and athlete pay rules. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said on the "Paul Finebaum Show" last week that "elections have consequences" and that the SEC is preparing for a future with or without the bill.
On Wednesday, the Knight Commission on Intercollegiate Athletics urged conferences to act on their own. It called on leagues to cap spending on coaching pay, buyouts, recruiting and facilities. They also asked to reserve a pool of conference revenue for schools that verify they follow the rules and to require every Division I school to disclose athlete compensation by sport. The commission said conferences should adopt its framework even if the PCSA passes."There is no excuse for inaction," Knight Commission co-chair Pam Bernard said.Time is running short on Capitol Hill, with only a two-week window and a de facto cram session facing House leadership aiming to bring the bill to the floor.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers There are plenty of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.  Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. The odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.               Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds             Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.               What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.              The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                         Win             The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                          Place             The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.              Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                           Show             A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                           Win/Place             Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                           Place/Show             The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                           Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)              Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.              It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                           The most popular horse racing bet types             Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).              It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.               Exactas             An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.  Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                           Trifectas             This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.              The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                           Superfectas             Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                          Super High 5             Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in other forms of sports betting.  The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                          Box             A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.              For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:             $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:             $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.              A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                           How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers             While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                           Daily Double             The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.              Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                           Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6             Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.             Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.              The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.  For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                           Understanding horse racing payouts             After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.              The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:             2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             				             $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				             If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.              For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:              2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				            Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting            The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.             January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes             Triple Crown of horse racing             The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.              Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.              The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                           Tips and advice for betting on horse racing             There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                           Racing forms and past performances             Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                           Track conditions             Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                           Horse tendencies              From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.              The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                           Post position             Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                          Trainer and jockey information             A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                           Workout times             There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                           Speed figures             Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.              Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                          Manage your horse racing betting bankroll             Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                           Rules and responsible gaming             Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.             Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts. title: Are the 76ers truly one of the NBA's best teams, or just one of the luckiest? - CBS Sports
description: Philly is 11-0 in clutch games and appears to be playing with fire
body:
Philly is 11-0 in clutch games and appears to be playing with fire
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As the old adage goes, if you play with fire, you're eventually going to get burned. But so far, the 76ers are burn-free as they improved to 11-0 in clutch games with a 121-116 win over the Magic on Wednesday. A clutch game is defined as a game in which the score is within five or fewer points in the final five minutes. In theory, these are supposed to be something close to coin-flip affairs. That's not entirely true. Some teams are better equipped for late-game dynamics, and the 76ers, with all their individual shot creators and ability to lock down defensively over high-leverage stretches, certainly appear to be one of them. But 11-0? It's notable enough to have even played in that many photo-finish games this early in the season (the league average is just over six clutch games so far), but to have come out perfectly clean on the other side begs the question: Are the 76ers, now 13-3, truly one of the best teams in the league, or have they simply been the luckiest? 
        
            
                NBA Power Rankings: The LaMelo Ball effect is being felt in two places; Lakers take top spot from Spurs
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Slow starts, big holesSo far, the 76ers have been outscored by 47 points in the first quarter, where they are shooting just 43% overall and 30% from 3, both bottom-five marks, with the 25th-ranked defense. It's putting them in a lot of early holes, as evidenced by the six double-digit deficits they have managed to overcome in victory so far. 
OpponentBiggest deficitFinal marginCleveland Cavaliers29 pointsWon by 8Toronto Raptors17 pointsWon by 11Orlando Magic17 pointsWon by 5Indiana Pacers13 pointsWon by 5Charlotte Hornets13 pointsWon by 5New York Knicks10 pointsWon by 6Up front, let's say that NBA leads are not what they used to be. Double-digit deficits can be, and often are, erased in minutes. Still, common sense dictates that consistently pulling off these kinds of comebacks is probably not a sustainable model for success. It's only working right now because ...Late-game dominanceThe 76ers get better as games go on, and they get awesome at the end. In fourth quarters, their defense gives up 10 fewer points per 100 possessions than it does in first quarters (from 117 to 107), and in crunch time they become a wall, surrendering just 94 points per 100 possessions over 29 clutch minutes. It's not just their defense. Look at Philly's offensive uptick in these clutch minutes so far, which they have won by 46 points to flip outcomes almost literally at the last minute. 
By the numbersFG%3PT%FT%ORTGOverall46.3 (12th)35.5 (14th)79.3 (11th)114.5 (13th)Clutch50.9 (3rd)52.2 (2nd)91.2 (5th)140.6 (3rd)Keep in mind that, with a sample this small, those clutch numbers are inflating the overall numbers to an even greater degree, further highlighting Philly's relatively pedestrian production throughout the meat of most games. Starting lineup strugglesIt's been well chronicled that Philadelphia's starting lineup -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe -- has been a negative unit: minus-4.1 per 100 with an abysmal 101.8 offensive rating, which would rank as the worst in the league. These are pretty hard numbers to wrap your head around considering the talent, and it's not as if there's been an on-ball power struggle, as would make sense given all these accomplished scorers trying to press the gas and pull back at all the right places and times. The roles have seemingly come together pretty cleanly, which would seemingly bode well for the unit's long-term prospects. All these guys can create one-on-one, draw doubles, generate leverage and get downhill. It is going to come down to making the shots that are being created by these individual advantages (it would be nice to see at least a little more off-ball movement), and for all their talent, outside of Maxey, this is just not a group of especially strong shooters. That said, it's not going to stay this bad for James, who's shooting 22% from 3, or Embiid, who's under 40% overall. Plus, one of the great strengths of this starting lineup is that it can be split and staggered so many ways. These four guys aren't playing together all the time, and the two-man units fare better. It allows everyone to rest throughout the game, which, it can be argued, is fueling the late-game energy. So what's the verdict?I'm not going to call too much of this luck. This is a resilient, confident team that stays in the fight for 48 minutes. They are not slacking off for 43 and then trying to flip a switch. They make tough shots and dig in defensively for mini stretches to stay within striking distance, and then close like maniacs. They're not going to stay perfect in these coin-flip games, but they are better equipped than most teams to win the late minutes. Same as the Lakers, who have two elite shot creators in Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves and are not 7-1 in clutch games accidentally. It was the same last year, when James was with the Lakers, who finished with six more wins than expected based on their net rating thanks to clutch performance. The Sixers have elite playmakers on both ends, so it shouldn't be surprising when they make plays. Look at this closing sequence against Orlando. Edgecombe (a total stud, by the way) bails out a dead possession with a deep 3 against a dwindling shot clock, creates a steal on the other end, and then James is the closer, first with the midrange jumper and then a drive-and-kick to an Anfernee Simons corner 3 for the dagger. 
That spurt turned a one-point Sixers deficit into a six-point lead in about 90 seconds. On the one hand, it's tightrope stuff with Edgecombe being a 33.8% 3-point shooter and hitting a grenade shot like that. On the other hand, he's a nerveless guy clearly built to make big shots, as we've seen a lot this season. Simons is a 41% guy from deep, and his presence is huge for this team because of that fact (the same goes for Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who has also been excellent). We know James can still get downhill and kick to shooters as a matter of routine, and as games grind down, this becomes exponentially impactful. Meanwhile, Maxey and Brown didn't even play, and those are Philly's two most reliable individual shot makers. Maxey alone gives the Sixers a leg up in just about any matchup as an impossible one-on-one cover given his unparalleled shooting/speed combo. Embiid is able to save defensive energy because they don't need to wear him out throughout games to win. They don't need to wear any of these guys out, in fact, even though they play big minutes. Again, it's not to say the Sixers are going to stay on a 66-win pace when their plus-2.1 CTG net rating pegs them as a 46-win team, but this is the way the Sixers are built to win -- by keeping games close with two star players on the court at all times, and then overwhelming opponents with sheer force and shotmaking down the stretch. It's certainly working so far.

        A season of poor headlines keeps getting worse for Michigan. This time, star receiver Andrew Marsh is in the news as he faces a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure stemming from an off-campus interaction with a female delivery driver, MLive.com reports.According to a press release from the Pittsfield Township Police Department, Marsh allegedly exposed himself when the delivery driver dropped food off at his residence. When the driver left, Marsh allegedly messaged her with an invite to return to his residence.The police department didn't name Marsh, but he was named in court records. Marsh's arraignment date has been set for Dec. 2. The maximum sentence for misdemeanor indecent exposure is one year in jail and a $1,000 fine.In a statement provided to MLive.com, Michigan football spokesperson Dave Ablauf said that the team is aware of the charge and is still gathering information.

"We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available, but we are unable to comment further due to the ongoing case."Marsh is in his second season with the Wolverines, and he's followed up a promising freshman campaign with some sophomore struggles. Marsh has posted 48 receptions for 459 yards and one touchdown, but that's still a slight step down from his 2025 production as the entire Wolverines offense has regressed.
It's not yet known whether this charge will affect Marsh's status for Saturday's game against No. 4 UCLA, although he was listed as questionable on Wednesday night's Big Ten availability report. If Marsh doesn't suit up on Saturday afternoon, that would be a significant loss for a Michigan offense that's struggling to find the end zone even with a full complement of weapons.

description: Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup

Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup

        In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts.Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot.The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline.Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Texans vs. Colts liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: NRG Stadium (Houston)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Colts have the ballThe Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL. Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions.
The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games.The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan, including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state.
When the Texans have the ballC.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season.The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner, either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins.It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. 
This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. PredictionI just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13

title: Clemson AD calls out 'disappointed' atmosphere during Georgia Tech loss: 'It's hard to be a part of that' - CBS Sports
description: Dabo Swinney may face more pressure to change as fan discontent reaches the ears of the AD
body:
Dabo Swinney may face more pressure to change as fan discontent reaches the ears of the AD
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:24 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Clemson's loss to Georgia Tech was another frustrating chapter in the era of Dabo Swinney, who hasn't adapted to the modern landscape of college athletics. Disappointment was palpable at Memorial Stadium, and athletic director Graham Neff admitted it was the worst atmosphere of his tenure.Neff has been at Clemson since 2013, starting as associate athletic director before being promoted to athletic director in 2022. In an interview with Tiger Illustrated, Neff said the product on the field and in the stadium overall left a lot to be desired."That was the most frustrated and disappointed atmosphere and feel within the stadium that I've experienced," Neff said. "And I think that would be consistent with most of the Clemson family that was there. And it was really hard. It's hard to be a part of that, and to feel that."What was transpiring on the field, with the injuries and dynamics of the game, in addition to all the other aspects in and around the stadium - the product on the field matters. The product in the stadium matters."
The groans and complaints from fans don't just emanate from anonymous internet trolls. Neff said real-life fans have expressed disdain for the overall Clemson football experience."We hear it," he said. "Not just stuff on social media, but fan feedback that we solicit at the games."The growing frustration amongst the fan base, which has clearly resonated with Neff, is at odds with the optimism that Swinney presents when faced with criticismr about the overall direction of the team.
Swinney doubles downDuring his weekly press conference on Tuesday, Swinney doubled down on his long-term vision for the program. Swinney predicted another national title for the Tigers during his tenure and pointed to his overall track record as reason to believe that will happen."Coach Swinney is gonna win another national championship," Swinney said. "... Little rough patch right here, but I'll work through it. If you don't believe in me, that's fine. I got 18 years of reasons why to believe. If you're gonna decide whether or not to believe in me after two seasons, that's fine."The issue is that Swinney won those national titles before NIL and the transfer portal were big factors in roster building. At the time, Clemson was bringing in elite recruiting classes without having to worry about major roster turnover every offseason.
In the modern era, Swinney has eschewed the transfer portal and made some head-scratching staff decisions. The latest was hiring Chad Morris as offensive coordinator, despite the fact that he hadn't worked in that role since 2020. Instead of looking toward the future, Swinney reached into his past for answers, and it backfired.In something of a departure from Swinney's philosophy, Neff told Tiger Illustrated that "what drives winning is different now." The Clemson AD added that the school will have to "continue to adapt in all aspects of the landscape."Neff asserted that his commitment to getting Clemson football back on track is unwavering.
"The change has been significant in the last five years, and our mindset needs to be that in the next five years it's going to continue to change significantly," Neff said. "That's being all-in. That's my job for Clemson football, but honestly for all of our sports."The question for the Tigers is their coach's ability to adapt. There's a chance Clemson finishes the regular season at 6-6, and 8-4 is the best possible outcome.The program is behind the eight ball in its approach to the transfer portal and NIL, and high school recruiting has slipped. Those things must change — one way or another — if the Tigers are going to be contenders on the national stage once again.

title: Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense - CBS Sports
description: Would adding a seasoned veteran like Irving really help the logjam at guard already in the Utah locker room?
body:
Would adding a seasoned veteran like Irving really help the logjam at guard already in the Utah locker room?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.On Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Why would the Jazz be interested in Kyrie?So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a new roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.Irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success. 
If they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.
Why this rumor makes so little senseThe question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they plan to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench. Adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever. 
Markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.There's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.And then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared plans to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.
Is there anything we can take from this?Sometimes a rumor says more about a team's big-picture plans than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.The simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered quickly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.Skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out. 
There may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.However, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.Ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

title: What Cowboys' Christian Parker said about demotion: DC considered leaving, pushed back on decision - CBS Sports
description: Parker mulled departing Dallas after Brian Schottenheimer took defensive play-calling
body:
Parker mulled departing Dallas after Brian Schottenheimer took defensive play-calling
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:52 pm ET

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys put first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker in a no-win situation.    Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer left Parker in a bizarre limbo state after stripping him of his defensive play-calling responsibilities and giving them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine for the rest of the season. Yet, Schottenheimer is keeping Parker on staff as the defensive coordinator to lead defensive meetings and build the defensive game plan. Teams regularly fire coordinators in-season, and they also let coordinators fight through adversity. Dallas did a little bit of both with Parker, which is certainly unique. That's why, when addressing the move on Thursday, Parker called his situation "not ideal." "Not an ideal situation for me personally, but it's what's best for the team at this current point," Parker said. "So that's how we're moving forward. Continuing to prepare and operate in the same way that we've been doing during the week to have the goal of winning on Sunday." 
Some coaches in Parker's shoes would have walked out the door after being essentially neutered professionally. Parker said he considered it as an option, yet he chose to stay. "I think you can always choose to do that, right? Yeah, exactly," Parker said. "[But] we didn't even get to the point of discussing that. I think initially it's going to stink, right? So initially in your mind, you're thinking about all the things and in my opinion, that would've been running from it."And at the end of the day, I got a job to do, and my job is to be the defensive coordinator of the Dallas Cowboys. Whether that is calling plays on Sunday, obviously that's not the case anymore, but on ... whatever day we play, there is a focus level that I need to have. There's a contribution that I still have to be able to maintain. That is regardless of feelings and anything else."
Parker, who at 34 is the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, made it clear that he lobbied hard with Schottenheimer to remain the DC with full responsibilities. But he said, "At the end of the day, that was a decision that was made."That decision came after another loss in Week 11 when Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in franchise history. In the aftermath of another frustrating defensive effort, the Cowboys now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).What's next for Dallas, ParkerParker confirmed everything Schottenheimer announced on Wednesday about his duties remaining the same during the week going forward, outside of play-calling responsibilities. What has also remained the same in Dallas over the years is the defense's inability to play sound football. 
Per CBS Sports Research, the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers. Schottenheimer saying Parker has a "very bright future here as our defensive coordinator" comes off as if he's talking about a first-round-pick quarterback he has to bench because the speed of the game is too fast. Schottenheimer disagreed that he is "benching" Parker, but Parker himself drew some parallels with his players in that regard. He pulled 2025 second-round pick edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku from the starting lineup in Week 6, and Parker said it would be hypocritical for him to have the same mature, steady attitude as a player when dealing with a similar demotion. 
"Yesterday when I saw Eze, he's like, 'Hey, remember what you told me?'" Parker said. "Because I told him, 'Look, this is changing at the start of the game. This has not changed the second, third, fourth quarter. It doesn't change anything that we expect from you when you go out on that field.'"So if I'm telling Eze that, how can I not tell myself that? And it's not about me, it's about this team."The timing for Parker is unfortunate because Dallas' next two games provided him a chance to rebound against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles. However, Parker doesn't see his situation that way. 
"There's never a right time for anything like this. So our focus is forward. It doesn't matter who we're playing."  Speaking of looking forward, Parker's future in Dallas is very unclear at the moment. Does he expect to return to the Cowboys as their defensive coordinator in 2027, like Schottenheimer said he believed he could? "We'll cross that bridge when we get there," Parker said.

title: MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Thursday, Nov. 19
body:
Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Thursday, Nov. 19
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 19, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1? In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive. Onto the rumors. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    D-backs price on Marte 'very high'It's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A big hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are said to be interested. Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some issues arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets to meet with TairaThe Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious. Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023. CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cubs scouting SatoThe Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic. Sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power. CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mariners not doneAfter being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.Further, he also said the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    White Sox looking for more rotation helpFresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.
Though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Nationals showing interest in rotation helpThe Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi. Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings. 
The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons. Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

James Madison will move from the Sun Belt to the American on July 1, 2027

        James Madison's departure from the Sun Belt to join the American will not take long, as the school announced on Thursday that the conference change would take effect on July 1, 2027. When the Dukes initially announced their intention to move conferences, they said it would happen by July 1, 2028 at the latest. But after working out an exit agreement with the Sun Belt, all parties decided it was best to wrap things up next year rather than let it drag out through 2027. "I would like to thank James Madison president Dr. James C. Schmidt and vice president and director of athletics Matt Roan for their work to arrive at a sensible resolution to James Madison's departure from the conference," said Sun Belt Conference commissioner Keith Gill. "We are thankful for their time in the Sun Belt and wish them the best in their future endeavors."
The Dukes will be the 15th football member of the American, which has not publicly indicated interest in adding another team to get to an even number of member institutions. With the news that James Madison will join quickly for the 2027 season, it seems likely that the American will spend at least one season with an odd number of programs. James Madison will try to end their Sun Belt tenure with another conference title, but it will need help to reach the conference championship game. The Dukes are on a bye this week before closing out their season at home against Coastal Carolina. A win there would improve them to 6-2 in conference play, and they will be rooting for Georgia Southern (currently 5-1 in conference play) to lose one of their final two games to Troy or Louisiana Tech -- with the Bulldogs currently the best team in the conference at 6-0. 
With James Madison beating Georgia Southern earlier this year, if they both end up 6-2, it'll be the Dukes representing the East division in the championship game against Louisiana Tech, which has clinched the West.
